sent_subject: SparrowHR: 3 focused tests for Import Employees + Pricing (with impact math you can plug in)
sent:
Samir —

You said the stall is at “import employees” and the pricing page. Looked only there. Three tests you can run fast, plus how to size impact against your own baselines.

1) Import: add an “Explore first” path before CSV/HRIS import (with sample data)
What to change
- On the first screen after signup, make “Explore SparrowHR” the primary action; keep “Import employees” secondary and always visible in nav.
- Offer “Try with sample data” so core screens (PTO, Reviews, Org) render immediately.
- Add a short reassurance line near Import; link your Security/DPA pages. If applicable, clarify what is or isn’t saved until confirmation.
Why it should help
- Reduces perceived commitment at the very first step and lets new users see value before doing admin work.
How to measure
- Import start and completion rates; Day‑1 activation (e.g., first PTO policy or first review cycle created); time‑to‑first key action.
Impact math (plug your numbers)
- Recaptured completes = visitors reaching import prompt × (drop‑off at that prompt) × (share who take Explore then return to import).
- Activation lift = recaptured completes × current post‑import activation rate.

2) Import: template‑first, visible auto‑mapping, and preview before commit
What to change
- Put “Download CSV template” and “Connect Gusto” upfront; show a mapping helper that auto‑detects columns with explicit, on‑screen confirmations.
- Allow a partial upload/preview to validate mapping and show a few rows before committing.
Why it should help
- Removes ambiguity (“will this field map?”) that causes abandonment or support pings.
How to measure
- Drop‑off on mapping; error rate per import attempt; retries per user; help‑chat volume on import topics.
Impact math
- Potential gain through mapping = visitors who start mapping × (drop‑off on mapping) × (share who succeed with preview + clearer mapping).

3) Pricing: swap “Prefer a walkthrough?” form for an immediate calendar; surface trial de‑risking at the CTAs
What to change
- Replace the multi‑field request form (which says replies take 1–3 business days) with a self‑serve calendar; keep the form as a fallback.
- Put “No credit card to start” copy directly beside each “Start 14‑day trial” button (you already use this line on Home); keep the “credit card required to activate after trial” note where it is.
Why it should help
- Removes the waiting period for high‑intent evaluators and reduces hesitation at the trial click.
How to measure
- From Pricing: click‑through to trial; booked‑demo rate; calendar no‑show rate vs. form submit rate.
Impact math
- Trial uplift potential = pricing visitors who reach tier CTAs × (non‑clickers at those CTAs) × (share influenced by adjacent de‑risk copy).
- Demo uplift potential = visitors who view the walkthrough block × (non‑submitters) × (share who book when a time is available now).

If you want the above as A/B specs (events, variants, and decision thresholds) we can write them to your current instrumentation in one pass. You’ll just need to drop in your step‑level baselines.
